title: Component projection estimates for leading Hilbert weights
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $r\ge4$, and let $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a connected closed subscheme with Hilbert polynomial $dm+c$, $d>3$, and $d/r<8/7$. Assume its reduced support $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is nondegenerate, meaning that no nonzero linear form vanishes on it. Use the weighted monomial and leading-coefficient convention of [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials]. Let $Y$ be a reduced irreducible component of degree $e$; put $W=\ker(k^r\to H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y(1)))$. Give $W$ weight zero and its quotient weight one, and put $s=\dim(k^r/W)$. If the local ring of $X$ at the generic point of $Y$ has length at least two [def-weil-pbc-module-length], then
$$s\le e+1,\qquad a_F\ge2e+\tfrac12.$$
If $X$ is generically reduced, $e\le3$, and $Y$ is not a rational normal curve, then
$$s\le e,\qquad a_F\ge e+\tfrac12.$$
These are statements about the displayed projection flags, without any semistability assumption. A rational normal curve of degree $e$ means a smooth rational curve whose embedding in its own linear span is the complete degree-$e$ embedding of $\mathbf P^1$. Component degrees below are degrees of the pulled-back hyperplane line on the smooth normalized components [def-sc-normalization, def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Section 3.2 proof of Theorem 8, steps (2)--(3), printed p.14; agent explicit leading-coefficient version of the component-projection estimates. The multiple-component estimate is the coefficient 2e+1/2 in Gieseker, Lectures on Moduli of Curves, Proposition 1.0.3, printed pp.30--36. Local PDFs WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials], $X$ has dimension one and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ has dimension $P(m)=dm+c$ for all large $m$. As a closed subscheme of projective space, $X$ is finite type over $k$. A field is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] give finitely many irreducible components. A zero-dimensional irreducible component would be a closed point, disjoint from every other irreducible component (otherwise it is contained in that component). Finiteness makes it open as well as closed, contrary to connectedness and dimension one. Thus $Y$ is one-dimensional. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-curve-span-degree-rigidity] to $Y$. It gives $e\ge1$ and $s\le e+1$; in the non-rational-normal case it gives $s\le e$. Apply [lem-sfb-component-primary-complement-separation] to $X,Y$, obtaining $\mu,Q,C,\delta$ with $\delta=d-\mu e\ge0$ and the ideal-power restriction injection. All these are fixed for this particular $X,Y$; no uniform bound in families is needed here.

source.place: Proposition 1.0.3, pp.30--33; Morrison Theorem 8 proof steps (2)--(3)

proof.text: In the multiple-component case $d\ge\mu e\ge2e$. If $e=1$, then $s\le2<r$; if $e\ge2$, then $r>7d/8\ge7e/4>e+1\ge s$. In the second case $s\le e\le3<r$. Thus $W\ne0$ in both cases. If $|X|=Y$, every form in $W$ would vanish on $X_{\mathrm{red}}$, contradicting nondegeneracy. Hence $Y$ is proper. The complementary-subscheme lemma now supplies $P\in Y\cap C$ on a one-dimensional component of $C$. In particular $\delta>0$, since a Hilbert polynomial with a one-dimensional component has positive linear coefficient. In the generically reduced case $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ is a reduced zero-dimensional local ring, hence a field; its length as a module over itself is one, so $\mu=1$.

source.place: Proposition 1.0.3, p.31 and the boundary choice on p.32; numeric hypotheses of the present item

proof.text:
Choose a basis compatible with $W\subset V=k^r$, and for $0\le j\le m$ let $E_j(m)$ be the span in $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ of restricted degree-$m$ monomials of weight at most $j$; put $\beta_j=\dim E_j(m)$. A monomial of this weight has at least $t=m-j$ factors in $W$, so belongs to $H^0(X,\mathcal I_Y^t\otimes\mathcal O_X(m))$. If $t\ge Q$, restriction to $C$ is injective on this space. Since every form in $W$ vanishes at $P\in Y$, its restriction to $C$ lies in the ideal of the reduced point $P$. Products of $t$ such forms consequently lie in $\mathcal I_{P,C}^t\otimes\mathcal O_C(m)$. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-point-power-section-bound] to $C,P$ to obtain, for all sufficiently large $m$ and $0\le j\le m-Q$,
$$\beta_j\le\delta m-(m-j)+K.$$
For the remaining $Q-1$ indices below $m$, use simply $\beta_j\le P(m)$.

source.place: Proposition 1.0.3, pp.32--34, the filtration ranks and point-ideal estimates

proof.text:
A minimum-weight monomial basis has exactly $\beta_j-\beta_{j-1}$ vectors of weight $j$, with $\beta_{-1}=0$: greedily extend a basis of each $E_{j-1}$ by monomials spanning $E_j$. Conversely every monomial basis has at most $\beta_j$ vectors of weight at most $j$, so its total weight is at least that of this greedy basis. Summation by parts gives
$$w_F(m)=\sum_{j=0}^m j(\beta_j-\beta_{j-1})=mP(m)-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\beta_j.$$
Step 3 bounds the latter sum by
$$\sum_{j=0}^{m-Q}(\delta m-m+j+K)+(Q-1)P(m)=(\delta-\tfrac12)m^2+O(m).$$
Here $Q,K,d,c$ are fixed; the equality is just $\sum_{j=0}^{m-Q}j=(m-Q)(m-Q+1)/2$. Therefore $w_F(m)\ge(\mu e+\tfrac12)m^2-O(m)$. The asymptotic expansion of [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials] forces $a_F\ge\mu e+\tfrac12$, by dividing by $m^2$ and letting $m$ tend to infinity.

source.place: Proposition 1.0.3, pp.34--35, summation of filtration ranks; same rank calculation with generic multiplicity one for Morrison step (3)

proof.text: When $\mu\ge2$, Step 4 gives $a_F\ge2e+1/2$ and Step 1 gives $s\le e+1$. When $X$ is generically reduced and $Y$ is not rational normal with $e\le3$, Steps 2 and 4 give $a_F\ge e+1/2$, while Step 1 gives $s\le e$. These are precisely the two asserted estimates for the specified zero/one flag. None of these steps invokes Hilbert semistability.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NP-d0ee6c35e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 5 steps, the 3 new unsplit nodes and every cited statement. Source: fetched Morrison arXiv:0810.2340 §3.2 and read pp.13-15 (Theorem 8 steps (2)-(3); e_F=2a_F convention). Both item estimates contradict semistability exactly when d/r<8/7: (2e+1/2)/(e+1)>=5/4 and 1+1/(2e)>=7/6. Gieseker's online copy was unreachable (HTTP 429), so I proved each new node myself. (a) Span rigidity is the classical minimal-degree theorem, valid in any characteristic; checked on a line, a conic, a twisted cubic and a plane cubic. (b) Primary complement: C=V(J), with J the intersection of the non-Y primary components; I_Y^Q is inside q_Y, so I_Y^Q meets J in 0; multiplicities are preserved off ξ; slope d-μe by degree additivity; P exists by connectedness and because there are no 0-dimensional components; C empty is consistent. (c) Point bound: split along a reduced component Z through P; the kernel has dimension at most P_N(m) and the image at most e_Z m-t+1, giving δm-t+K for all t<=m. Item steps: W≠0 case analysis (e=1, e>=2, e<=3) correct; ideal inclusions correct; greedy-basis summation by parts gives a_F>=μe+1/2. Sharp on xy=0 (3/2) and x^2y=0 (5/2). No duplicates found (checked linear-series bound, subcurve-span, interpolation, Lasker, Riemann-Roch nodes); no node restates a clause of the item. Batch-5 finding: lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension reaches lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function, which is Stacks 00K1 generic graded Hilbert polynomial. It is not a statement or proof step of the trace formula or Poincare duality, and Step 2 uses it only for δ>0, so the citation is accepted. Tool uses accepted: two generic Mathlib leaves (finite-type over Noetherian, finitely many components). No SGA. Advisory: the point-bound node does not link def-weil-irreducible-components. No changes.
